svg.text: Reasoning Models — Black Box to White Box
DeepSeek-R1 · Chain-of-Thought · GRPO training · Test-time compute
① From outside: one API call, one token stream
{model: "deepseek-r1:8b", prompt: "Hur många sekunder är det på ett år?", stream: true}
Token stream — everything generated in one continuous session:
The model is NOT called once per reasoning step.
All tokens — including every calculation inside <think> — stream from ONE generation session. No orchestration.
Why writing steps helps (Wei et al. 2022 — arXiv:2201.11903):
Each token is predicted conditioned on ALL prior tokens in the stream.
When the model writes "365 × 24 = 8 760", that value enters the KV-cache.
Every later token attends to it — the calculation becomes part of the working context.
More reasoning tokens = more intermediate compute = better answers on hard problems.
Test-time compute scaling (Snell et al. 2024 — arXiv:2408.03314)
Longer reasoning traces = more "compute at inference". Trading latency for accuracy.
Same insight as "think step by step" prompting — but baked into the model weights via RL training.
② Inside the transformer — autoregressive KV-cache loop
← token appended to cache, next iteration starts
KV-cache: why reasoning tokens are "free" to reuse
Once "8 760" is cached, all future tokens attend to it at zero extra cost — it's already in memory.
The longer the reasoning trace, the more facts the final answer token can "see". No recomputation.
Simplified attention: token "sekunder" attends strongly to earlier calculated values
8 billion parameters · 32 transformer layers · 4096 hidden dim · 32 attention heads
GGUF Q4_K_M quantization: weights stored in 4-bit integers → ~5 GB on disk, same architecture
deepseek-r1:14b 14B params · 40 layers · ~9 GB Q4 → use when 8b gets the reasoning wrong
Standard SFT models learn to mimic (prompt→answer) pairs. Reasoning models learn via RL: emit a trace, get rewarded only if correct.
Group Relative Policy Optimization loop (arXiv:2402.03300, arXiv:2501.12948):
Key insight: the model is never told what a "good" trace looks like.
It discovers useful reasoning strategies purely from outcome rewards. The trace emerges from the policy, not supervision.
More stable signal, harder to scale
Reward only the final answer correctness
Simpler, scales well with GRPO sampling
Also relevant: PPO (Schulman et al. 2017 · arXiv:1707.06347) — the earlier RL algorithm GRPO improves upon.
CoT paper: Wei et al. 2022 · arXiv:2201.11903 — showed chain-of-thought emerges in large models.
④ When the model IS called multiple times
These require an external orchestrator calling the Ollama API in a loop. Ollama does NOT do this on its own.
Works well for math/factual tasks where there's one right answer. Cheap wins via sampling diversity.
Tree of Thoughts — Yao et al. 2023 · arXiv:2305.10601
Branches reasoning into a tree. Evaluates intermediate states. Prunes bad branches.
Each node = one model call. Needs a separate evaluator (also the LLM) to score partial solutions.
Dramatic gains on creative writing, planning, puzzles where CoT alone fails.
Requires Python orchestrator calling /api/generate in a loop. Not built into Ollama.
